title: Monoclonal Antibody Therapies in Chronic Inflammatory Diseases: Periodontal Outcomes, Oral Safety and Clinical Implications—A Scoping Review
content: Monoclonal antibody-based therapies are widely used in chronic immune-mediated diseases, yet periodontal effects, dentoalveolar safety signals and exposure characteristics remain incompletely characterized. This scoping review mapped periodontal outcomes, safety signals, administration, exposure and pharmaceutical-context reporting in adults. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched in July 2026 without publication-year or language restrictions. Sources were selected using Population, Concept and Context criteria, appraised with design-specific Joanna Briggs Institute tools and synthesized by therapeutic target. Of 1154 records, 21 reports representing 20 studies or cohort families were included. Evidence concentrated on rheumatoid arthritis and therapies targeting tumour necrosis factor, interleukin-6 receptor, cluster of differentiation 20, or interleukin-17A. Tocilizumab showed the most consistent reductions in gingival inflammation and bleeding on probing, whereas structural changes were smaller and inconsistent. Tumour necrosis factor-directed findings were heterogeneous; small rituximab studies showed favourable clinical or biomarker signals, while pharmacovigilance contained infectious and destructive dentoalveolar signals. Intravenous and subcutaneous administration were represented, but exposure reporting was incomplete. No included periodontal study evaluated formulation stability, storage, cold-chain integrity, or handling deviations. Risk-based periodontal surveillance may accompany therapy, but validated protocols cannot be defined. The identified gap concerns integrating pharmaceutical-context variables into periodontal research, not monoclonal-antibody stability research generally.
